issues.description: The supplied do-file has comments naming four Excel loads, then uses/reshapes already-loaded variables without any import command. Workbook paths, sheets, header rows, source ranges, imported variable names and the exact working-days source/definition are absent. These are unresolved input contracts; no import syntax or replacement field definitions are inferred.

The regional and HQ preparation sections use subsidiaries_merged1.dta before the later supplied merge block creates it. The producer is present, so this is a supported run-order preparation step, not an absent empirical input; execute the regional/HQ blocks after the first merge in a working copy.

The code sorts monthly observations by subsidiary or region plus year/month and forms target, headcount and working-day lags with [_n-12], then retains years from 2011. The datasheet documents monthly data and actual-sales years 2007–2016, but does not establish the exact target, headcount or working-days period, continuity, missing-month pattern, or uniqueness of the joined keys. Therefore it is unknown whether row twelve earlier is the intended prior-year month for all input series. Preserve the authored boundary behavior: the code does not explicitly require a nonmissing lag for every first retained observation, and no extra years are inferred beyond actual code needs.

The do-file derives sub_region as substr(sub_id,1,3) and later merges the working-days table on sub_region/year/month. The datasheet describes counts per region but gives no mapping from the official webpage's region identifiers or labels to these code-derived keys, so join compatibility and the precise working-day definition remain unresolved.

After that producer, run the regional block at lines 154–205 and retain its clear all at line 208 between the regional and HQ sections. Then run the HQ block at lines 211–257 and retain its clear all at line 260 before the headcount merge section.

Enter the headcount merge section at lines 293–303 from empty memory: the existing use at line 297 opens subsidiaries_merged1.dta.
